reasoning: The evidence shows the Fed held rates at 3.5-3.75% in January 2026. As of early 2026, most forecasts expected 2-3 rate cuts for the year, likely starting in June or later. Snippet 9 from February 2026 shows growing expectations for 3+ cuts due to cooling inflation (2.4% YoY in January). However, multiple sources indicate the Fed is unlikely to cut in the first half of 2026, with BOCI explicitly stating low probability of cuts before H2. The April meeting (April 28-29) falls in this cautious period. Market expectations from January showed only ~15.5% probability of any cut by March. Given the Fed's data-dependent stance and preference to wait, a 25 bps cut specifically at the April meeting appears unlikely.
